text:
Logan Stankoven won a Stanley Cup with Carolina in June, and the 23-year-old has started the defense of it like a man in a hurry: 11 goals and 21 points in 22 games, on only 16.7 minutes a night. Per 60 minutes, that is 3.43 points, far above the 2.04 to 2.81 range our numbers think he can sustain.

Some of it is luck. The Hurricanes have scored 7.3 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. But the chances are not luck. Carolina takes 64% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five-on-five with him out there, seven points better than without him, and his own 1.53 expected goals per 60 is well up on last season's 1.14.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains how a 5'8" winger does it: 7.2 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net, 91st percentile. Evolving-Hockey adds a fair caveat: he plays with very strong teammates, which flatters raw numbers. His minutes dipped to 15.5 over the last ten. Watch whether they come back.
headline: Stankoven's chances are as real as his points
